To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Escherichia glycerol kinase has been crystallized in three forms suitable for X-ray structural analysis and that these crystals diffract to 1.8-3.0 A. The
Escherichia Coli Glycerol kinase, an enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of glycol with ATP, has been crystallized in three forms.
the enzyme is a homodimer in solution and in the crystal and that the enzyme crystallizes in three different crystal forms, all with high symmetry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the three-dimensional structures of the enzyme and the identification of residues involved in the binding of glycerol, ATP and ADP.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for the regulation of glycerol kinase by glycerol.
the structural analysis of the Escherichia Coli glycerol kinase (ECK) and the elucidation of the structural changes which accompany its catalytic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme is a dimer in the asymmetric unit of the first crystal form and a tetramer in the asymmetric unit for the second crystal form.
the enzyme is a dimer and the tetramer is a crystallographic artifact.
glycerol kinase crystallizes in a variety of forms, which are suitable for X-ray analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization of glycerol kinase is not a trivial problem.
the glycerol kinase crystals are suitable for X-ray diffraction analysis at high resolution and that they may be used to determine the molecular structure of the enzyme.
we have obtained three different crystal forms of E. coli glycerol kinases which diffract to high resolution and which appear to be suitable as targets for X-ray crystal structure studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallization of a protein in a complex with an inhibitor or activator can be used to stabilize the protein in a specific conformation.
the crystallization conditions for E. coli glycerol kinases can be optimized to yield crystals of different forms that diffract to high resolution.
we were able to crystallize the glycerol kinase enzyme from E.coli and we have been able to get diffraction data to 1.8 angstroms resolution.
